subject.title: Feature request: Add Gateway received timestamp to inbound metadata for accurate latency tracking

question: Should OpenClaw add a generic Gateway receive timestamp to agent-visible inbound metadata, and what field name, timestamp format, and propagation boundary should be canonical?
rationale: Source inspection proves the gap, but choosing the public field semantics and propagation boundary is a product/API decision automation should not invent.

options.title: Define Generic Receive-Time Contract
options.body: Add an additive cross-channel field with documented semantics and tests that prove source timestamp and Gateway receipt timestamp remain distinct.

options.title: Keep Timing Internal
options.body: Expose receive-to-dispatch timing in logs or diagnostics instead of adding agent-visible prompt metadata.

options.title: Defer To Channels
options.body: Let individual plugins add timing where needed, accepting less consistent cross-channel latency analysis.

recommendation.title: Define Generic Receive-Time Contract
recommendation.body: Add an additive cross-channel field with documented semantics and tests that prove source timestamp and Gateway receipt timestamp remain distinct.

likelyOwner.reason: This product/API question is closest to adjacent message metadata work and the prior timestamp-metadata close path.
